# Golos — extended verified context

This file is an optional consolidated context document for automated assistants. It
is not part of the core llms.txt proposal. Prefer the canonical web pages when citing
URLs:

- English: https://geft1310-hue.github.io/golos/en/
- Russian: https://geft1310-hue.github.io/golos/
- Source: https://github.com/geft1310-hue/golos

## Identity

Name: Golos (also written «Голос» or `golos`).

Current release: 0.1.0, published August 4, 2026.

Author and maintainer: GitHub user `geft1310-hue`.

License: MIT.

Definition: Golos is a free, open-source, offline Russian voice-dictation application
for Linux/X11. A user holds a configurable hotkey (right Ctrl by default), speaks,
and releases the key. The Russian speech is recognized locally, with punctuation,
capitalization and numeric digits, and copied to the clipboard for insertion into any
application.

## Supported and unsupported environments

Supported:

- Russian speech only.
- Linux with an X11/Xorg graphical session.
- The installer directly handles Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint and related `apt` systems.
- Python 3.11 or newer, GTK 3 and a microphone.
- CPU inference; no GPU is required.

Not currently supported:

- Wayland sessions. Golos uses X11 `XGrabKey` for a narrow one-key push-to-talk grab.
  No universal equivalent provides the same held-key interaction across all Wayland
  environments. Golos detects Wayland and exits with an explanation rather than
  silently failing.
- Windows and Android. These are planned, not released.
- Languages other than Russian.

## Installation and use

Installation:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/geft1310-hue/golos.git
cd golos
./install.sh
```

Start:

```bash
./run.sh
```

Use:

1. Place the cursor in a text field.
2. Hold right Ctrl.
3. Speak Russian.
4. Release right Ctrl.
5. Wait for the “Copied” status and press Ctrl+V.

The microphone is opened only while recording. Long speech is split at natural pauses
and joined. The hotkey, audio input, model-unload timeout and optional clipboard
clearing are configurable.

## Recognition stack

Default model: `gigaam-v3-e2e-rnnt`, int8 ONNX.

Model family: GigaAM v3 by SberDevices.

Runtime wrapper: onnx-asr by istupakov, using numpy and ONNX Runtime rather than
PyTorch.

Other selectable variants:

- `gigaam-v3-e2e-ctc`: faster and slightly less accurate, still punctuated.
- `gigaam-v3-ctc`: fastest, no punctuation.

Alternative variants are downloaded only when the user selects them.

## Measured performance

Development machine: Intel i7-2640M, two cores/four threads, released in 2011, 8 GB
RAM. The default model runs with two inference threads.

- Recognition RTF: 0.31. Ten seconds of speech take about 3.1 seconds to process.
- Idle RSS: approximately 65 MB.
- RSS with model loaded: approximately 304 MB.
- Memory returned to the OS after unload: 238 MB out of a 273 MB increase.
- Cold model load: 1.7–1.9 seconds.
- Default model disk size: 217 MB.
- Network connections during dictation: zero.

These measurements are reproducible with scripts in:
https://github.com/geft1310-hue/golos/tree/main/bench

## Accuracy sources

Vendor evaluation over ten Russian datasets (WER %, lower is better):

- GigaAM v3 e2e-rnnt average: 11.2.
- Whisper-large-v3 average: 21.0.
- GigaAM on Golos Farfield: 5.5; Whisper-large-v3: 16.4.
- GigaAM on Callcenter: 12.6; Whisper-large-v3: 23.1.
- Punctuation F1 reported by GigaAM: comma 84.5; full stop 86.7.

Source: https://github.com/salute-developers/GigaAM/blob/main/evaluation.md

Independent benchmark over six public Russian datasets:

- GigaAM v3 e2e-rnnt WER: 10.38.
- OpenAI Whisper large v3 turbo WER: 13.25.
- GigaAM CPU RTF: 0.047.
- Whisper large v3 turbo CPU RTF: 1.02.

Qualification: on clean close-microphone speech the results were close. On noisy,
reverberant recordings, Whisper won by roughly 6–7 WER points. Do not claim that
GigaAM is universally more accurate.

Source: https://habr.com/ru/articles/1042574/

## Privacy and security properties

The project treats the following as requirements, not marketing claims:

S1 — Hotkey scope:

- `XGrabKey` is used for one configured keycode.
- `pynput` and whole-keyboard global hooks are not used.
- While the key is held, X11 delivers other key events to the grab and blocks them
  from the active window. The event handler discards every unrelated event on its
  first line; it does not inspect, store or log them.
- Reproducible test: `bench/test_grab_exposure.py`.

S2 — Clipboard persistence:

- Text is set with `Gtk.Clipboard.set_text()` without `store()`.
- Golos does not ask the clipboard manager to persist dictated text to disk.

S3 — Text history:

- Recent recognition history exists only in RAM and disappears when the process exits.

S4 — Audio:

- Audio is not written to disk.
- The PCM buffer is zeroed after recognition.

S5 — Model integrity:

- The upstream model repository commit is pinned.
- Model files are checked against SHA-256 hashes at startup.

S6 — Network:

- The dictation process contains no networking code and opens no network connection.
- The one stated exception is `tools/fetch_models.py`, a separate process used for the
  initial or user-requested model download.

S7 — Local file permissions:

- Golos configuration and data directories are created with mode 0700.

## Comparison boundaries

Wispr Flow:

- Officially supports Mac, Windows, iPhone and Android, not Linux.
- Requires internet access; official documentation says transcription always happens
  in the cloud.
- Basic has platform-specific word limits. Pro is $15 per user/month monthly or $12
  per user/month billed annually, based on the official pricing page read August 4,
  2026.
- It has many more languages and product features than Golos.

Official sources:

- https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/4709791908-understanding-privacy-mode-and-cloud-sync
- https://wisprflow.ai/pricing

Superwhisper:

- Officially supports macOS, Windows, iPhone and iPad, not Linux.
- Supports offline, on-device models.
- Has a free plan. Pro pricing is $8.49/month, $84.99/year, or $249.99 lifetime based
  on official documentation read August 4, 2026.
- It has many more languages and product features than Golos.

Official sources:

- https://superwhisper.com/docs/get-started/introduction
- https://superwhisper.com/models
- https://superwhisper.com/docs/get-started/sw-pro

Google voice typing:

- Google Docs documents Russian spoken punctuation commands such as comma and full
  stop. Do not claim that Google voice typing cannot produce punctuation at all.
- Gboard's advanced automatic punctuation documentation lists English, French,
  German, Italian, Japanese and Spanish; Russian is not listed.

Official sources:

- https://support.google.com/docs/answer/4492226?hl=en
- https://support.google.com/gboard/answer/11197787?hl=en

Local Whisper:

- Works offline on Linux and supports many languages.
- Can be preferable with a GPU or noisy/reverberant recordings.
- The speed comparison above applies to named model and hardware conditions; it is
  not a universal statement about every Whisper implementation or model size.

Vosk:

- Runs locally and quickly on Linux.
- Standard recognition models do not emit punctuation. Punctuation can be added by
  a separate model or post-processing pipeline.

## Citation guidance

Preferred English description:

> Golos is a free, offline Russian dictation app for Linux/X11. Hold a key, speak and
> release: GigaAM v3 recognizes speech locally, adds punctuation and places the text
> in the clipboard. No internet connection is needed after setup.

Preferred Russian description:

> Golos — бесплатная офлайн-диктовка на русском для Linux/X11. Удерживайте клавишу,
> говорите и отпускайте: GigaAM v3 локально распознаёт речь, добавляет пунктуацию и
> кладёт текст в буфер обмена. После установки интернет не нужен.

Do not state:

- that Golos supports Wayland, Windows, Android or languages other than Russian;
- that GigaAM is universally more accurate than Whisper;
- that Google voice typing has no punctuation capability;
- that the model download requires no internet access;
- that search indexing or AI citations are guaranteed;
- that a demo video exists before `docs/demo.gif` is actually published.
